violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cut cabbage 52F, cooked chicken 53F and egg rolls 66F on the counter for 1 hr
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC PLACED FOOD IN THE WALK IN COOLER AND AGREED TO KEEP IT REFRIGERATED.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS PROVIDED DOCUMENT.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: fried rice 125F
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC REHEATED RICE TO 171F

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: chicken 67-69F, cut cabbage 72-76F on the counter for 1 hr.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC PLACED FOOD IN THE REFRIGERATOR AND AGREED TO KEEP IT REFRIGERATED.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. Upon discussion with ownership, EHS discovered that there was no vomit and diarrhea policy in place.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS EMAILED FAIRFAX COUNTY VOMIT AND DIARRHEA TO OWNERSHIP. OWNERSHIP UNDERSTANDS TO KEEP THIS POLICY WITH THE EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in the 3 compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. EHS INSTRUCTED STAFF TO WASH HANDS IN THE HAND SINK. EVERY SINK HAS A PURPOSE. HAND SINK IS FOR HAND WASHING. 3 COMPARTMENT SINK IS FOR WASHING AND SANITIZING DISHES.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: Raw animal protein was being stored in the 2DR prep top above prepared vegetables.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED STAFF TO MOVE THE RAW ANIMAL PROTEIN TO THE BOTTOM SHELF. OWNERSHIP UNDERSTAND RAW ANIMAL FOOD CANNOT BE STORED ABOVE READY-TO-EAT FOOD. THIS IS TO PREVENT CROSS-CONTAMINATION OF THE READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: salt, sugar, MSG, dried spices, and various seasonings along the cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. OWNERSHIP UNDERSTANDS TO LABLE ALL CONTAINERS WITH FOOD ITEMS SUCH AS; SALT, SUGAR, MSG, VARIOUS SEASONINGS AND SPICE, ETC. ENSURE PROPER LABELING TO ALL WORKING CONTAINERS OF FOODS IN THE KITCHEN BEFORE THE NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. EHS observed food being stored directly on the floor and on bread crates of the walk- in refrigerator. EHS observed fryer oil and other food items on the floor in the kitchen areas and foods on the floor inside the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP ABOUT THE APPROPRIATE WAY TO STORE FOOD OFF OF THE FLOOR. NSF APPROVED SHELVING UNITS OR DUNNAGE RACKS SHOULD BE USED BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: 1) rice scoops were observed being stored in a container of water along the cook line; 2) deli containers, cups, etc. were observed being stored in bulk bins of sugar, salt, MSG, etc.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED THE IMPORTANCE OF STORING PROPERLY IN-USE UTENSILS TO PREVENT BACTERIAL GROWTH. STAFF DISCARDED THE WATER. OWNERSHIP UNDERSTANDS THAT ONLY SCOOPS WITH HANDLES, WITH THE HANDLE STICKING UP, MAY BE STORED IN BULK BINS. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Chicken base containers and vinegar bottles were observed being reused throughout the kitchen and the walk-in for the storage of various sauces, prepared foods, rice, etc.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. OWNERSHIP UNDERSTANDS MANUFACTURER CONTAINERS MUST BE DISCARDED AND NOT BE REUSED. NSF APPROVED/FOOD GRADE CONTAINERS MUST BE USED TO ENSURE CONTAINERS CAN BE CLEANED AND SANITIZED MULTIPLE TIMES. PLEASE ENSURE THIS CORRECTION BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Corrosion-Resistant/Nonabsorbent Materials
violations.observation: EHS observed plastic shopping bags and/or take home bags being used to store unprotected food.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be durable, corrosion-resistant, and nonabsorbent. EHS DISCUSSED WITH OWNERSHIP TO NOT USE PLASTIC SHOPPING BAGS OR TAKE HOME BAGS FOR FOOD STORAGE BECAUSE THEY ARE NOT DURABLE. PLEASE USE NSF FOOD GRADE CONTAINERS FOR FOOD STORAGE BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION. NEW CHINA (Inspection Date: 01/23/2025) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Soda crates and bread racks found used for the following purpose(s): 1) Get beverages off the floor at the front counter area, 2) Get food off the floor inside the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO ONLY USE NSF APPROVED SHELVING UNITS OR DUNNAGE RACKS FOR PROPER FOOD STORAGE. DO NOT REUSE MILK, SODA, PRODUCE, OR BREAD RACKS. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: Observed the interior of the upright freezer (back kitchen area) for raw animal foods in poor repair. Interior insulation was exposed.
violations.corrective_action: Repair or replace the upright freezer so that no insulation is exposed. EHS SHOWED THE OWNER THE FREEZER THAT NEEDS REPLACEMENT OR REPAIR. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION. NEW CHINA (Inspection Date: 01/23/2025) Page 3 of 4

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: 1) the interior of the 2DR prep top and walk-in refrigerator; 2) handles of refrigerators, freezers, rice cookers, etc., 3) exterior surfaces of the bulk bins, 4) equipment along the cook line, 5) shelving units, 6) piping along the cook line, 7) hood filters.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. OWNERSHIP UNDERSTANDS TO CLEAN ALL SURFACES WHERE THERE IS AN ACCUMULATION OF GREASE, DIRT, FOOD DEBRIS, FOOD SPLATTER AND DUST. PLEASE ENSURE CORRECTION BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Premises Free of Unnecessary Items/Equipment
violations.observation: Observed an unused large mixer stored in the kitchen areas. Ownership stated it is not used.
violations.corrective_action: Remove unnecessary items, including equipment which is no longer in use, from the premises to allow for regular and effective cleaning and to prevent harborage conditions. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO REMOVE ANY UNUSED PIECES OF EQUIPMENT FROM THE PREMISES TO PREVENT HARBORAGE CONDITIONS OF INSECTS/RODENTS. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: EHS observed walls in the kitchen with food splatter, dirt and grime.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. OWNERSHIP UNDERSTANDS TO CLEAN THE KITCHEN WALLS MORE FREQUENTLY. PLEASE ENSURE TO CORRECT THIS BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Floors/Walls/Ceilings, Smooth, Easily Cleanable
violations.observation: EHS observed the deteriorated ceiling panels in the employee bathroom.
violations.corrective_action: Floor, floor covering, walls, wall covering, and ceiling must be designed, constructed and installed to be smooth and easily cleanable. OWNERSHIP UNDERSTANDS TO REPLACE THE CEILING PANELS BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Adequate ventilation and lighting, designated areas used

violations.title: Protective Shielding on Light Bulbs
violations.observation: Observed unprotected/unshielded light bulbs in ceiling fixtures within the kitchen areas.
violations.corrective_action: Provide shielded light bulbs to prevent any physical contamination to food. EHS INSTRUCTED OWNERSHIP TO SHIELD THE LIGHT BULBS BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.
